text:
**The answer is D, battery.** Battery can be based on criminal recklessness, and the defendant admitted he was indifferent to the consequences of driving recklessly, so injuring the pedestrian makes him guilty of it. The team note is wrong on this point: attempt requires a specific intent to commit the crime, so attempted manslaughter based on recklessness is generally not recognized, and the defendant denied any intent to injure, which rules out A and C as well.

CONFIDENCE: 88
